name: SavvyCal
tagline: Scheduling links with overlay calendars and nicer booking UX

pricing.notes: Official pricing checked 2026-07-30; Basic listed at $12/month monthly and $10/month annually.

tiers.name: Basic
tiers.limits: Unlimited calendars, scheduling links, team scheduling, and meeting polls.

tiers.name: Premium
tiers.limits: Everything in Basic plus custom domains, delegated access, paid bookings, and branding removal.

pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (2 months free); 30-day money-back guarantee
pricing.hiddenCosts: Paid bookings require Premium; Stripe or other payment-processing fees still apply.

verdictSummary: The core booking-link loop can be cloned, but calendar reliability, time-zone correctness, reminders, and polished link UX make it more than a trivial script.
coreLoopDIY: Read availability, generate shareable scheduling pages, write booked events, and email confirmations.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay for a nicer, reliable scheduling experience that avoids friction with guests.

priorArt.name: Cal.com
priorArt.desc: Open-source scheduling platform covering the main booking-link mechanics.

alternatives.name: YouCanBookMe Free
alternatives.desc: One booking page, but it keeps forms, payments, confirmations, polls and the calendar-overlay trick.

alternatives.name: zcal Free
alternatives.desc: The booker sees calendar conflicts on the page, and free also buys unlimited links, forms, reminders and polls.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Cal.com Free
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Excellent free scheduling, but no equivalent overlay-calendar booking experience.

notes: Good smaller-brand page; open-source prior art makes the verdict nuanced.
prompt:
Build me a solo booking page to replace SavvyCal: one person, one calendar, a few link
types. Requirements:

- Node + Express + better-sqlite3 on my VPS behind HTTPS; server-rendered pages, Luxon
  for timezone math.
- Link types in links.json: slug, title, duration, buffer, allowed hours (e.g. /intro,
  30-min slots, 15-min buffer, weekdays 10:00-16:00 my time).
- Availability from Google Calendar free/busy (googleapis, OAuth creds in .env); show
  open slots for the next 14 days in the visitor's detected timezone with a timezone
  switcher.
- Booking form: name + email + note. On submit, create the event on my calendar with the
  guest as attendee so Google sends the invite, and store the booking in SQLite.
- Re-check free/busy at submit time, not just render time, so two guests cannot grab the
  same slot.
- Confirmation email to guest and me via Resend or SMTP (creds in .env), including a
  cancel link that deletes the event.
- No accounts, no telemetry beyond my own server logs.
- Out of scope: team links, routing, payments, and reminder sequences. One calendar,
  mine.
- README: the Google Cloud console OAuth steps (budget an hour, it is the worst part)
  and the DNS/HTTPS notes.
